h1: How Should a Cap and Gown Fit?
keywords: how should a cap and gown fit
how should a graduation gown fit
how are graduation gowns supposed to fit
how should a gown fit for graduation
how should a graduation cap fit
how is a graduation cap supposed to fit
how is a cap and gown supposed to fit
answer: A graduation gown fits when it hangs loosely from your shoulders with room to layer clothes underneath, the hem falls between mid-calf and a few inches above the ankle, the sleeves reach about your wrist, and it zips without pulling. The cap should sit flat and level, about an inch above your eyebrows.
intro: Academic gowns are meant to be roomy, so they look the same on everyone in the procession. Sizing is usually based on your height, sometimes with weight or build, rather than chest measurements. Try it on as soon as you get it, over the clothes you plan to wear, so there's time to exchange it if it's badly off.

checklist.good: The gown rests on your shoulders with the yoke seam at or slightly past the shoulder edge. It drapes straight down from there.
checklist.tooTight: The yoke pulls across your upper back and the shoulders strain when you reach forward.
checklist.tooLoose: The shoulders slide down your arms and the neckline drops off your neck at the back.

checklist.good: The zip or snaps close easily over your clothes, with a few inches of room across the chest so the front hangs smoothly.
checklist.tooTight: The front closure pulls or won't fully close, or the gown strains across the chest when you sit.
checklist.tooLoose: This is rarely a problem; gowns are meant to be full. Only worry if the front sags open or drags.

checklist.good: With arms relaxed, the sleeve opening reaches roughly to your wrist so it doesn't ride up when you shake hands or hold a diploma. Bachelor's sleeves are pointed and longer at the back.
checklist.tooTight: Too short: sleeves end above the wrist or ride up to your forearms when you raise your arm.
checklist.tooLoose: Too long: the sleeve covers your hands and gets in the way when you hold your diploma.

checklist.good: The hem falls between mid-calf and a few inches above your ankle, with your shoes on.
checklist.tooTight: Too short: the hem sits at or above the knee, which looks like the wrong size from the audience.
checklist.tooLoose: Too long: the hem brushes the floor or catches your heels on steps and the stage.

checklist.good: The neckline sits close around your neck without pressing. A hood or stole lies flat over it.
checklist.tooTight: The neckline chokes or pushes up against your throat when fastened.
checklist.tooLoose: The neckline gapes or slides back, showing your clothes and letting the hood or stole slip.

checklist.good: The body falls loosely in folds from the yoke with room to walk and sit without pulling.
checklist.tooTight: The gown clings to your hips or stretches across your seat when you sit.
checklist.tooLoose: Excess fabric balloons out at the sides or pools around your feet.

variations.heading: High school, bachelor's, master's and doctoral gowns
variations.intro: Academic dress follows a common pattern in the US. The fit checkpoints are the same, but sleeves and extras change with the degree.

items.name: High school
items.text: A simple, usually shiny gown in school colors with a matching cap and tassel. Fit by height, and check the hem in your graduation shoes.

items.name: Bachelor's
items.text: Long, pointed sleeves and a closed front. Black is traditional. Wear it closed, with a stole, cords or medals if your school allows them.

items.name: Master's
items.text: Oblong sleeves closed at the bottom, with a slit for your arm near the elbow. The sleeve end hangs below your arm. Worn with a hood lined in your school's colors.

items.name: Doctoral
items.text: Bell-shaped sleeves with three velvet bars, velvet front panels and often a velvet tam instead of a mortarboard. The gown is fuller and heavier, so check you can move your arms freely.

items.name: Taller or broader builds
items.text: Order by height first, then check whether the maker has a plus or big-and-tall option. A gown sized only by height can strain across the chest or shoulders for broader frames.

measure.heading: How to measure for a cap and gown
measure.intro: Most schools and regalia companies ask for height, sometimes weight, and head size for the cap. Measure accurately: guessing on height is the main reason gowns end up the wrong length.
steps: Measure your height without shoes, standing straight against a wall. Note it in feet and inches, such as 5′6″.
If asked, give your weight or build. Some makers use it to add width through the body.
For the cap, wrap a soft tape around your head about ½ in above your eyebrows and ears, where a hat would sit. Note the measurement in inches or centimeters.
Add the height of the shoes you'll wear if they're very tall heels; some size charts ask you to choose the next size up.
Order by the deadline so there's time to swap sizes.
measure.tip: If you're between two gown sizes, choose the longer one. A slightly long gown is less noticeable than a short one, and you can wear slightly taller shoes.

problems.problem: The gown is a few inches too long
problems.fix: Wear slightly taller shoes, or have the hem temporarily taken up with a basting stitch or iron-on hem tape. Don't cut it if it's rented.
Ask the school or regalia supplier for an exchange. There's no practical way to lengthen a gown.

problems.problem: The cap slides off or tilts backward
problems.fix: Wear your hair lower, away from the crown, and use bobby pins through the elastic or headband on each side.

problems.problem: The gown is creased from the package
problems.fix: Hang it in a steamy bathroom or use a handheld steamer. If you iron polyester, use the lowest setting with a cloth between iron and gown.

problems.problem: The hood or stole keeps slipping
problems.fix: Pin the hood cord or the stole to your shirt or dress at the front and back with small safety pins.

extra.heading: How a graduation cap should fit
extra.body: The mortarboard should sit flat and level on your head, about 1 in above your eyebrows, never tipped back like a baseball cap. Many caps have a point at the front of the skullcap; that points to the middle of your forehead. The cap should feel snug enough to stay put when you nod, but not tight. Most caps have an elastic band; fitted caps are sized by head circumference. In many US schools, the tassel starts on the right and moves to the left after degrees are conferred, but follow your school's instructions.

extra.heading: What to wear underneath
extra.body: Gowns are often made of polyester and can be warm, so wear light layers. Shorter skirts and dresses should not show below the gown hem; knee-length or shorter works well. Choose comfortable, stable shoes that you can walk in on stairs and a stage. Dark socks and shoes look neat under black gowns.

extra.heading: Hoods for graduate degrees
extra.body: The hood drapes over your shoulders with the velvet trim lying around your neck and the colored lining turned out at the back. A small cord or loop at the front attaches to a shirt button or is pinned so the hood doesn't pull back against your throat. Ask a classmate or your department to help you adjust it the first time.

picks.label: Handheld garment steamer
picks.why: The quickest way to get packaging creases out of polyester gowns without risking iron damage.

picks.label: Bobby pins and small safety pins
picks.why: Keep the cap secure and the hood or stole from slipping during the ceremony.
picks.query: bobby pins and safety pins set

picks.label: Graduation cap insert or grip band
picks.why: Helps the cap stay level and comfortable, especially with thick or styled hair.

faqs.q: How long should a graduation gown be?
faqs.a: Between mid-calf and a few inches above your ankle, measured with your graduation shoes on.

faqs.q: How should a graduation cap fit?
faqs.a: Flat and level about an inch above your eyebrows, snug enough to stay on when you nod. The point of the skullcap goes at the front.

faqs.q: Are graduation gowns supposed to be big?
faqs.a: Yes. They're cut loose and full so they drape over your clothes. The sleeves and hem should still be the right length.

faqs.q: What if my graduation gown is too long?
faqs.a: Wear slightly taller shoes or have the hem taken up temporarily. Avoid cutting a rented gown.

faqs.q: How do you keep a graduation cap on?
faqs.a: Wear your hair low and push bobby pins through the cap's elastic band on each side and at the back.

faqs.q: Which side does the tassel go on?
faqs.a: In many US ceremonies it starts on the right and moves to the left after degrees are conferred. Your school will tell you its custom.
